question: For Warrant 1 Condition A with at least two major-street lanes and one minor-street lane, what volumes must exist and over what time basis, and does meeting them compel signal installation?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For Condition A with 2 or more major-street lanes and 1 minor-street lane, Table 4C-1 (100% columns) requires 600 vehicles per hour on the major street (total of both approaches) together with 150 vehicles per hour on the more critical minor-street approach (one direction only), existing for each of any 8 hours of an average day. Meeting these volumes does not compel signal installation: the provision is Guidance stating only that the need for a signal "should be considered" based on an engineering study. Standards (mandatory): - "These major-street and minor-street volumes shall be for the same 8 hours for each condition; however, the 8 hours that are selected for the Condition A analysis shall not be required to be the same 8 hours that are selected for the Condition B analysis." - "These major-street and minor-street volumes shall be for the same 8 hours for each condition; however, the 8 hours satisfied in Condition A shall not be required to be the same 8 hours satisfied in Condition B." Guidance (recommended): - "The need for a traffic control signal should be considered if an engineering study finds that one of the following conditions exist for each of any 8 hours of an average day: A. The vehicles per hour given in both of the 100 percent columns of Condition A in Table 4C-1 exist on the major street and the more critical minor-street approach, respectively, to the intersection; or B. The vehicles per hour given in both of the 100 percent columns of Condition B in Table 4C-1 exist..." - For the combination of Conditions A and B (after adequate trial of other remedial measures), the 80 percent columns apply: for this lane configuration, 480 vph on the major street and 120 vph on the minor-street approach for Condition A, in combination with the Condition B 80 percent values, for each of any 8 hours of an average day. Options (permitted): - "Any four consecutive 15-minute periods may be considered as 1 hour if the separate 1-hour periods used in the warrant analysis do not overlap each other and both the major-street volume and the minor-street volume are for the same specific 1-hour periods." - Per the table footnotes, the 70 percent columns (420 vph major / 105 vph minor for this configuration) may be used when the major-street speed exceeds 40 mph or in an isolated community with a population of less than 10,000, and the 56 percent columns may be used for the combination of Conditions A and B under the same speed/population conditions after adequate trial of other remedial measures. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 4C-1, Condition A, row "2 or more / 1" shows major-street volumes of 600 (100%), 480 (80%), 420 (70%), and 336 (56%) and minor-street volumes of 150, 120, 105, and 84, with footnotes explaining when the reduced-percentage columns apply. Citations: - Section 4C.02 Guidance §4 (p.653) - Section 4C.02 Standard §5 (p.653) - Section 4C.02 Guidance §9 (p.654) - Section 4C.02 Standard §10 (p.654) - Section 4C.01 Option §15 (p.652) - Table 4C-1 (p.653)
gold_answer: For each of the same 8 selected hours, 600 vph must exist on the major street (both approaches total) and 150 vph on the critical minor approach (one direction) at the 100-percent thresholds. Meeting the warrant does not compel installation; an engineering study must determine whether a signal is justified.
